# Documentation (generated by experiments/generate_docs_index.py — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `experiments/generate_docs_index.py` on 2026-11-24 at commit 530ff46-dirty from configs/documentation_registry.json, configs/moved_paths.json, configs/study_sheet_diagrams.json, each registered document's first lines; do not edit by hand.

This project builds a signed, typed physiology graph (genes and the proteins they encode, metabolites and reactions, signalling, transcription, electrical and drug-mechanism layers, brain cell classes) and models how a perturbation, an allele of a gene or a drug, propagates through it to psychiatric symptom constructs, so that the learned mechanisms can serve as the basis of a new psychiatric nosology. The [repository README](../README.md) is the overview; this page is the map of the documents.

Each document has a class, which says how far to trust it as a statement of the present ([documentation process](documentation_process.md)): **living** documents are kept current and reviewed; **records** are dated and corrected only by dated additions; **generated** documents are written by the script they name and carry its stamp; **frozen** documents are pinned by their hash; **drafts** await the owner. What is current is in [status](status.md), not in memory.

## Where documents live

Each class has its place, so the top of `docs/` holds what is kept current and a document's folder says how far to trust it ([documentation process](documentation_process.md#where-documents-live-20-november-2026)). A file keeps its name when it moves.

- `docs/`: the documents kept current (living), the frozen registration baseline, the process pages (this page, status, the file index, the decision and amendment histories, the registered rules), the running logs (the decision log, the label source review, the development sessions, the data-layer rebuilds) and the bibliography.
- `docs/generated/`: every page and data file a script wrote, with the inputs a page's script reads beside the page; never edited by hand.
- `docs/records/<YYYY-MM>/`: dated records, in the month the register says each was recorded, with their attachments.
- `docs/drafts/`: text awaiting the owner.
- `docs/figures/, docs/study_sheet_figures/`: the figures that figures.md and study_sheet.md show.

**A new document** goes where its class puts it from the start: a living document at the top of `docs/`, a record in `docs/records/<YYYY-MM>/` for the month it is recorded, a page or data file a script writes in `docs/generated/`, a draft in `docs/drafts/`, and a table the graph or evidence build reads in `configs/`. `python experiments/register_documents.py --add-missing` prints the place for a new Markdown document, and `tests/test_documentation_process.py` fails for a registered document anywhere else, and for a file left at the top of `docs/`. The owner chose folders by class on 20 November 2026 ("1 class") and, asked whether `CLAUDE.md` should say where a new document goes, answered "either there or the readme" and then, asked on 21 November 2026 which of the two, "Whichever makes more sense to you": it is this page, where a person goes to find or add a document, so the rule is stated here and in the [documentation process](documentation_process.md#where-documents-live-20-november-2026).

58 files have not moved yet: phase 2 waits until no work in flight, and nothing awaiting the owner, holds a file the move must edit, phase 3 (the build inputs) waits for the next data-layer rebuild, and `configs/moved_paths.json` lists each with its place. An old path, as a record or the decision log may still write it, is in the [moved-files table of the file index](file_index.md#moved-files) with its new path and the date of the move.

## Contents

One row per topic below, counting its documents by class. Within a topic the living documents come first, then the records (newest first, with the date each was recorded), drafts, frozen copies, the generated pages that carry the provenance stamp, and last the generated pages written before the stamp existed (16 October 2026), which are history: read them as the state of their date, not as the current graph or model.

A script that wrote the same page for several runs has its versions on one line. The current member of such a family is the one generated on the tables the registered model reads, v5 (the owner, 20 November 2026, "Version families"); the register marks it, and a family whose line says no member is on those tables has no current member, every version of it being history until one is regenerated.
